title: Modi Interacts With AI Avatar of Swami Chinmayananda at Chinmaya Anniversary
excerpt: The holographic avatar greeted the Prime Minister at Bharat Mandapam, reviving his 1993 Vadodara meeting with the late Chinmaya Mission founder.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacted with a holographic AI avatar — a "Holobot" — of Swami Chinmayananda at the inauguration of the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on October 23.
  • The avatar greeted him "Hari Om, Narendra!"; Modi called the experience "very emotional," saying it transported him 33 years back to his 1993 meeting with Swamiji in Vadodara.
  • Modi recalled inviting Swamiji in 1993 to the Chicago centenary of the Parliament of the World's Religions; Swamiji died in San Diego on August 3, 1993, before the event.
  • Amrit Mahotsav youth volunteers covered 40,000 km over 300 days and engaged more than one lakh young citizens, the official release said.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has interacted with a holographic artificial-intelligence avatar of Swami Chinmayananda, the Chinmaya Mission founder who died in 1993, at the inauguration of the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi — an encounter he described as an emotional return to a meeting 33 years earlier.

The avatar, described as a "Holobot" in coverage of the event, greeted the Prime Minister with "Hari Om, Narendra!", visible in the subtitles of the official video shared from the event. According to the Prime Minister's official release, the interaction transported Modi back to his 1993 meeting with Swamiji in Vadodara. "For me, this is a very emotional experience," he said. NationPress reported that Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat shared the video, calling it an "extraordinary confluence of faith and modern technology."

"For me, this is a very emotional experience."

— Narendra Modi, on the AI avatar interaction (PMIndia release)

The 1993 meeting behind the moment

Modi recalled that in February-March 1993 he visited Swamiji to invite him to Chicago for the centenary of the Parliament of the World's Religions, marking 100 years since Swami Vivekananda's address. Chinmayananda rallied support across America for the event but passed away in San Diego on August 3, 1993, before it took place. Their final conversation, Modi said, centred on youth power: "Its main essence was the building of youth power, and building a strong and capable India through youth power!"

The anniversary program

The Sammelan marks 75 years of the Chinmaya Movement. The official release said Amrit Mahotsav youth volunteers covered 40,000 km over 300 days and engaged more than one lakh young citizens, and that the Mission runs over 100 educational institutions. At the same inauguration, Modi called for unity against divisive forces and linked the 2047 Viksit Bharat goal to the Mission's centenary period — remarks covered separately in our earlier report from the Sammelan.

Why it drew attention

Devotional organisations hold deep archives of a teacher's recorded voice and image, and AI tools can now turn those archives into interactive figures. The Chinmaya Mission presented the Holobot as a set-piece within its anniversary program, not a replacement for living teachers — but a prime ministerial conversation with a digital recreation of a teacher dead for three decades gives the experiment unusual visibility, and raises the standing questions of who scripts such an avatar and how faithfully it can speak for its subject. The Mission runs Bala Vihar classes, temples and study groups across North America, making the anniversary directly relevant to diaspora Hindu families.
